UNPACKED SEMINAR / VOL. 002

From AI for Biology to Virtual Cells

From biological foundation models to virtual cells: approaches and limitations in cell-state representation, multi-omics integration, genetic perturbation prediction, and cell dynamics.

Session 2 · In Chinese

7 Nov, 10:00 Beijing (UTC+8)Tencent Meeting
Open Tencent MeetingAbout the talk

Live discussion only · No recordings or replays

Session 002 · English posterView full size ↗

01 / THE TALK

About the talk

AI for Biology · Virtual Cell · Biological foundation models · Single-cell multi-omics

Artificial intelligence is reshaping research in the life sciences, moving biology beyond traditional data analysis and pattern discovery toward the prediction, generation, and simulation of complex living systems. From protein structure prediction and design to genomic modeling and single-cell multi-omics analysis, AI for Biology is showing considerable potential across biological scales. This talk will first review the main technical advances and research paradigms in AI for Biology, then focus on virtual cells. It will cover cell foundation models, multi-omics data integration, genetic perturbation prediction, and cell dynamics, using representative studies to examine the modeling approaches, use cases, and limitations of different methods.

Discussion topics

01

AI for Biology: paradigms and trends

Review AI applications in proteins, genomics, and single-cell biology, with a focus on biological foundation models and generative models. Discuss what modeling approaches share and how they differ across biological scales.

02

Virtual cells: core tasks and approaches

Explore cell-state representation, multi-omics integration, genetic perturbation prediction, and dynamic trajectory modeling through representative studies. Compare the strengths and limitations of data-driven, mechanistic, and hybrid approaches.

03

Challenges and future research directions

Discuss limitations in generalization, causal inference, dynamic simulation, and cross-scale modeling. Explore the potential of high-throughput perturbation experiments, active learning, and mechanistic constraints in building verifiable virtual cells.

Suggested background · No specific background required

What you can take away

Gain a systematic understanding of the main research directions in AI for Biology and technical advances in virtual cells, including the use cases and limitations of different modeling paradigms. Understand the central scientific questions and technical challenges in moving from cell foundation models toward virtual cells, to inform future research topics and methodological choices.

02 / THE SPEAKER

About the speaker

Zhengyang Zhao

PhD Student

Academy for Advanced Interdisciplinary Studies, Peking University

AI for Biology · Genomics · Bioinformatics

Zhengyang Zhao is a PhD student at the Academy for Advanced Interdisciplinary Studies, Peking University. His research lies at the intersection of artificial intelligence and biology (AI for Biology), with a focus on genomics, bioinformatics, and AI applications in the life sciences. He has worked as a research assistant in several laboratories at Peking University and Tsinghua University. He was selected for the PhD student track of the China Association for Science and Technology’s Young Science and Technology Talent Development Program.

03 / THE HOST

Department of Engineering Mechanics, School of Aerospace Engineering, Tsinghua University

AI for PDEs · Computational solid mechanics

A PhD student in Engineering Mechanics and a Future Scholar at Tsinghua University. His research connects artificial intelligence with physics-based computation (Physical AI), focusing on AI for PDEs and computational solid mechanics.
